definition: Without meaning to, usually because of a lapse in attention.
example: While cleaning out the closet, she inadvertently donated the jacket with her keys still in the pocket.
nuance: Inadvertently suggests an oversight or a moment of inattention, while accidentally can describe pure chance with no lapse at all.
prompt: Students are typing group messages about their weekend plans.
options: Rushing to reply, Maya inadvertently sent the plans to her whole class instead of one friend.
After rereading it twice, Leo inadvertently sent the invitation exactly as he had intended.
Priya inadvertently hinted at the surprise party by mentioning cake, hoping her friend would guess.
Sam inadvertently promoted the club car wash in the chat, just as the club had asked him to.
reasons: Sending a message to the wrong people in a hurry is an unplanned slip.
Rereading carefully and sending as intended describes a fully deliberate act.
Hoping someone will catch a hint makes it purposeful; this confuses the word with indirectly.
Doing what you were asked is intentional; the word has nothing to do with advertising.

practice.prompt: A hiker is walking along a muddy forest trail.
options: The hiker felt it would be inadvertently to cross the swollen creek, so she turned back.
Distracted by a woodpecker, the hiker inadvertently wandered off the trail into some nettles.
After checking the forecast, the hiker inadvertently packed extra socks in case of rain.
The ranger inadvertently warned the group about the washed-out bridge, exactly as his job requires.
reasons: This mistakes the word for inadvisable; it describes unplanned actions, not unwise ones.
Drifting off course while distracted is an unintended result of not paying attention.
Packing for rain after checking the weather is a planned, conscious choice.
A warning given on purpose as part of one's duties is not an accident.
